figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Structural characterization of StvirS. a) Ribbon representation of StvirS (brown) in complex with the substrate analogue GFSPP (carbon:
green, phosphorus: white, oxygen: red, sulfur: gold, nitrogen: blue, Mg2+: black spheres, flexible regions: dotted lines; PDB ID: 9RS2) reveals a class
I terpene synthase fold. The isoprenoid ligand adopts a serpentine like conformation. b) The active site is shown with the corresponding Fo-Fc
electron density map for GFSPP (3.0 σ, ligand omitted for phasing); a stereo view is provided in Figure S1c. c) Superposition of StvirS:GFSPP with
CyS:GGPP (PDB ID: 7Y88),41 SdS:2,3-DHFPP (PDB ID: 4OKZ),47 and MibS:2-FGPP (PDB ID: 3V1X).48 These structures share conserved
overall topologies (Cα rmsd <0.8 Å) but differ significantly in substrate pocket height, while the width is moderately conserved and the depth
remains constant (∼5 Å). d) Surface slices of StvirSapo (light cyan; PDB ID: 9RRZ) adopting a partially closed intermediate state, and e) the closed
StvirS:GFSPP-bound conformation. f) The structural overlay depicts identical positioning of Gly184 (acting as the cation-stabilizing dipole) and
Arg180 (pyrophosphate (OPP) sensor), while the NSE triad (purple) undergoes minor adjustments. In contrast, significant rearrangements are
observed in the Asp-rich motif (ARM, blue). These conformational differences are due to the absence of Mg2+ ions in the apo state, which are
essential for coordinating the OPP moiety and promoting active site closure.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Site-directed mutagenesis of StvirS. Relative in vitro production of terpene products by StvirS variants, determined by GC/MS. Wild-type
total product yield was set to 100%. Bars represent means from triplicates; standard deviations are listed in Tables S2 −S5. Coelution of
compounds 1/10, 3/4, and 3a/6 prevented individual quantification. Inactive variants V57L/I303Y, D227N, and I303D are not shown.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Structural basis for product profile modulation. Binding
mode of the C25 prenyl chain in the StvirS:GFSPP complex (PDB ID:
9RS2) with selected residues targeted by mutagenesis. Superposition
with StvirSapo (PDB ID: 9RRZ; cyan), StvirS_V57Lapo (PDB ID:
9RS4; gray, L57 in magenta) and StvirS_I303Yapo (PDB ID: 9RS5;
light gray, Y303 in purple) shows uniform side chain positioning,
indicating a rigid specificity pocket. Product profile changes arise from
single side chain substitutions.
